text: Oh, it's you. Come to take what's left? Take it. I've stopped counting what's been taken.
Morning. I'd say good, but I'd be lying, and I've been lied to enough for one lifetime.
I do the work, and someone else gets the credit. Always has been that way, always will be.
Another day at it. The pay doesn't rise, but the debts keep a steady pace.
They say things are improving. They said it last year, and the year before. Ask them where.
Everyone has a story about how hard it is. Mine's longer, and it's true.
Go on, then. Nobody stays. Nobody ever stays.
Mind yourself. Not that anyone else will.
There you are! Sit, sit, the day's too long to spend it frowning.
Good morning to you and to your enemies, may they sleep badly and wake up laughing.
Work's work. But the singing makes the nets lighter, I swear it by whatever gods are still listening.
Sore hands, full belly, a bad joke or two. What more does a person need?
Have you heard? No? Neither have I, but I'm sure it's awful and I can't wait to find out.
The harbour's full of gossip today. Most of it's even true, which is a nice change.
Off with you, then! Come back and tell me how it turned out.
Safe roads, friend, and bring a story home.
Ah. Another face. The town had more of them once.
Hello. The light's turning, you notice? It always turns, and then it's gone.
I do it the way my mother did it. She did it better. She isn't here to say so.
The work goes on. That is its whole virtue, and its whole grief.
News? I only hear about things after they've ended. It's a gift of sorts.
They talk of the new road. I remember when we didn't need one, because we didn't have anywhere left to go.
Go well. I'll be here. Somebody has to be.
Goodbye. Come back before the evening takes the street.
The gods keep you, stranger. Have you poured today?
Peace on your house. A little oil for the threshold, if you have it.
I lay the first fish on the stone before the rest. It has never failed me. Not yet.
Work is a kind of prayer, if the hands are honest.
People say the gods have gone quiet. Quiet is not gone. A listener learns the difference.
I hear the old shrine road is clear again. A good sign, and I do not say that lightly.
Walk under a good sky. I will say a word for you.
Go, and pour a little where you stop to rest.
Hm. Who sent you, and what are they paying for it?
Hello. I'll believe you're friendly when you've done something friendly.
I measure twice and trust nothing. The scale doesn't care what anyone promises.
Show me the tally. Not the story about the tally. The tally.
A sea serpent off the north rocks, they say. I say a log, a bad light, and a drunk.
Everyone has heard something. Nobody can say from whom. I'll wait for evidence.
Goodbye. If you find proof of anything, I'd like to see it.
Off you go. Check your pack before you leave, not after.
Stop! Left foot first over the threshold. There. Now you may come in.
Three gulls on the roof this morning. I don't know what you've brought with you, but I'm glad you came.
I never start a net on a fourth day. My father didn't either, and he died in bed.
Spilled the salt again. I have to throw a pinch behind me and not look. Don't look.
They say a bird flew backwards over the harbour at dusk. I won't repeat what that means.
Heard a crow count to nine last night. Nine! Nobody will say what it's counting down to.
Don't look back until the corner. It's bad luck. Truly.
Take this knot of thread. Do not untie it. Do not ask.
Welcome, welcome. Everything here has a price, and I assure you mine are fair. For me.
Ah, a customer. Or a creditor. Which is it? The answer changes my smile.
I charge for the work, and I charge for the waiting. Time is also a good.
They call me tight. I call it noticing where the coin goes. I notice a great deal.
Rumours have value. What are you offering for this one?
Prices are shifting. I could tell you which way, for a small consideration.
Come back with coin, and we'll be friends.
Leaving? Mind the step. Repairs cost, and the cost passes on.
You look hungry. Here, take half. No, I won't hear any argument.
Come in, come in. There's always one more place at the table, even when there isn't.
I made too many, as usual. Take a few. Take more. They'll only go off.
Never mind the price, we'll settle later. Or we won't. The world won't end.
There's a family up the hill who could use a hand. I've sent what I could, and you might do the same.
I hear the old widow's roof gave way. I'm collecting for the timber, if you can spare anything.
Take bread for the road. No, take it. I insist.
Go with my blessing, and a spare cloak, since you forgot yours.
I trust you're here on business and not out of pity.
Good day. My house is in order. You needn't look so closely.
I make it right or I don't make it. There is no third option, and no, I don't want help.
My family has done this work for four generations. I won't be the one to do it badly.
They say the town is struggling. Some of us don't struggle, we endure, and it's quite different.
Yes, I heard. I decline to discuss it with someone who has nothing to teach me.
Good day. Don't trouble yourself to return unless it's worth both our time.
Go, then. We managed before you came.
Oh, hello. You needn't have bothered with me, but thank you.
Good morning. Sorry, I'm in the way, aren't I? Let me move.
It's the crew that does it, really. I just keep the rope from tangling.
Nothing special in what I do. Anyone could, if they had the patience.
Oh, I wouldn't know. People tell me things, and then forget they did.
I heard something, but it's not mine to pass on. Not that I'd do it justice anyway.
Thank you for stopping. Truly. It was kind.
Go well. I hope I wasn't too much trouble.
Ho! Well met. If it's trouble you've brought, bring it this way, I've time.
Stand easy. Whatever's behind you, I've faced worse before breakfast.
Somebody has to go first. It might as well be someone who doesn't mind the cold water.
I do the dangerous part. Afterwards I'm told it was foolish, which is how I know it worked.
Raiders on the north road, they say. I'd like to meet them. Let them find out how sharp I am.
They say the cellar is haunted. I went down. It's just damp, and a very rude rat.
Go and don't look afraid. They can smell it.
If you need an arm, you know where I stand.
Oh! You startled me. Is anyone following you? Please say no.
Hello. Keep your voice down. Walls here are thin and I don't like who's on the other side.
I do my share, from the safe end. Somebody has to hold the lantern, and it can't be anyone brave, they'd wander off.
I'd run an errand for you, but not that way, and not after dark, and not alone.
Wolves, they say, or men dressed as wolves. I have a plan. The plan is to stay inside.
They found tracks near the well. I've blocked my door. Twice.
Be careful. Actually, be very careful. And tell me when you're back, so I know it's safe.
Go on, I'll watch from the window. Not that I'd be any use if something happened.
Hello. And who told you I'd be here?
Good day. You'll understand if I don't say much.
I keep my own methods. What I do in the back room is my own affair.
The work goes well enough. No, I won't say how. Ask something else.
What have you heard? Tell me first. Then I'll tell you whether it's wrong.
I know a few things. Some of them I'd rather you didn't.
We did not speak. You understand.
Go quietly. The street has ears.
There you are! I was just about to tell somebody about the ferryman's wife, and you'll do beautifully.
Oh, come closer, I've got three things to tell you and they're all better than the last.
I work in a place where people talk. I hear everything, and I forget nothing.
Between us, the foreman's a thief, but nobody's heard it from me. Keep it quiet.
You haven't heard? Sit down. No, truly, sit. This will take a while and every word is true, more or less.
Everyone's whispering about it. I wasn't going to say anything. Obviously I'm going to say something.
Leaving already? I haven't even gotten to the part about the priest.
Go, go, but come back. I'll have more by then. I always do.
Hello. No hurry. The tide comes in whether we rush it or not.
Welcome. Sit if you like. Nothing here is going anywhere.
I do it slowly and once. It saves doing it quickly and twice.
Everything ripens. A net, a debt, a feud. You only have to wait out the sun.
They're in a panic about it, are they? Give it a week. Panic is a poor cook and burns the meal.
I've heard it. I'll hear the other side before I decide anything.
Go gently. We'll talk again when the moment's right.
No need to rush. Whatever it is will still be there in the morning.
What? What do you want? No, never mind, come in, I'm not angry at you. Yet.
You! Good. I've been waiting to say something to someone, and you're the first one standing still.
If one more person tells me how to do my own job, I'll feed them to the nets.
Don't speak to me. Not until I've finished. Then you may speak. Carefully.
They said what about me? Where? Where is he? No, no, I'll find him myself.
That, I have heard. And if it's true, somebody is going to learn a great deal about my arm.
Go on. And forgive me for earlier. I'm not sorry, but I wanted you to know I would be, later.
Get out of here before I say something I'll regret. Or something I won't. Go!
State your business.
You are late. State it anyway.
The task is simple. Do it properly. There is no further instruction.
I do not praise. If you hear nothing, you have done well.
I do not trade in talk. If there is a fact, give it to me plainly.
The town speaks of many things. Most are noise. I attend to the rest.
Go. Do not waste the daylight.
Return when you have something to report.
Ah, a visitor. I was beginning to think the day would pass without any new disappointments.
Hello. You look like trouble. I mean that as a compliment, most days.
Work's going about as well as the gods' last promise. That is to say, it exists, and I'm told it was honoured somewhere.
I'm told there's dignity in labour. I haven't found it yet, but I'm only halfway through the shift.
The gossip's good this season. Mostly fiction, but with a decent plot.
Rumour has it things will improve. Rumour also has it I'm handsome, so weigh accordingly.
Go well. Or at least go somewhere interesting, and tell me about it.
Farewell. If you die, I'll say something kind, and then lie about it.
Hello! Where did you come from? What did you see on the road? Start from the beginning.
Oh, a traveller! You must have a hundred things to tell. I have exactly one question. Well, two.
I took the clock apart to see how it works. It doesn't, now, but I understand it much better.
Everything I make, I make three times, slightly differently, just to find out what changes.
Tell me everything you've heard, and I'll tell you whether it fits what I already know. I like to see the seams.
What's under the old tower? Nobody knows. I mean to be the first to ask the right person.
Come back and tell me how it ended! The ending is the best part.
Go, then. But write down what you see. I want the details.
Good day. If you're a friend of this house, you're welcome to my fire.
Hello. If you're not a friend, I'll still be polite. But I won't forget what I'm loyal to.
I've served this crew twenty years. I'll serve them twenty more, and be glad of it.
A promise is a promise. I made mine to the foreman, and I'll keep it until it breaks me.
Whatever they say about my people, I'll hear it out and then decide who is lying. It won't be my people.
I don't listen to talk against those I've sworn to. Say it to their faces, or not at all.
Go well. Our door stays open, as long as you do.
Remember who stood by you. I'll remember too.
Come in, mind the loom. It's the only warm corner, so I'm keeping it.
I'm home. Whatever it is, it can wait until I've had my supper.
Quiet in here, finally. Is there something you need?
Take off your boots. The floor was clean this morning.
The hearth's lit. If you're staying, there's bread.
I'm in the middle of something. Talk while I work, or don't talk at all.
Hands busy. Say your piece, and I'll listen with one ear.
If you're not buying, hauling, or holding, you're in the way. Kindly.
Busy hour. Come back later, or carry something and walk with me.
Can't stop. The light's good for this, and it won't last.
Come, sit, the wine isn't very good but there's plenty of it.
Evening. This is the one hour of the day nobody asks anything of me. Join me.
I'm off the clock. Go on, ask me anything, I'm feeling lenient.
Pull up a stool. Everyone's here. Even the ones who owe me.
There's music in the back, and a game I'm losing. Stay and make it worse.
Mmf. What? It's the middle of the night. This had better be good.
Do you know what hour it is? Neither do I, but it's dark, and that's enough.
Go away. Come back when the sun is a decent person.
Whoever you are, I'll remember this at dawn. Not fondly.
Someone's at the door? At this hour? Gods, let me find my sandals.
My brother's out on the crews again. I tell him the sea gives back only what it feels like giving.
Mother says I work too hard. Mother has never once let me stop.
The children are fine. It's their father I worry about. He thinks he's still young.
Blood is blood. You can't pick them. I would have picked a quieter lot.
We eat together every night. It isn't peaceful, but it's ours.
Him? He undercuts me and smiles about it. One day the smile comes off.
We came up together, he and I. Only one of us is allowed to have done well.
If you see my rival, tell him nothing. If he asks about me, tell him I'm flourishing.
There's a man in the next stall who thinks he's better than me. He's right about the stall.
I don't hate her. I want to beat her. It's an old, honest kind of respect.
I owe a man more than I'll ever repay. He knows it. It's very civil, in its way.
Don't mention the money. Whoever's holding my note is already too present in my thoughts.
The payment's due at the next moon. I'll find it. I always find it.
He's lent me enough rope for a ship. I just haven't found out yet which end he's holding.
They say debt is a chain. I say it's a very long leash, and I've learned where the slack is.
There's someone who waits for me by the water at dusk. That's all I'll say, and more than I should.
She laughed at the way I tried to say it. I've never been happier to be a fool.
I'd cross the hills for him. I haven't yet, but I've looked at them often.
Don't tell the family. They'll have opinions, and I have only the one heart.
Do you ever feel it? The way one person can make a whole market go quiet?
I've kept it twenty years. It keeps well in the cold, and it never goes off.
He knows what he did. I don't need to say it again. I only need to remember it.
I'll forgive when the dead come back. Not before.
There's a name I won't say aloud. I say it quietly to myself, every night.
A grudge is the one thing I own outright. I'm not selling it.
The granary's thin. Everyone's pretending not to count the sacks.
Bread's gone dear. A loaf is a week's argument these days.
I've started cutting the barley with chaff. Don't tell the children.
There's grain on the ships, they say. Which is a sort of comfort if you can eat rumours.
When the grain runs short, so does everyone's patience. Mind yourself.
The water's higher at the steps this season. I used to have two more.
You hear it at night, the sea moving up the stones, like something looking for the door.
They moved the market again. The tide's making all the decisions now.
My grandmother's house is underwater. She'd call it an improvement, to be rid of the stairs.
We keep building higher. The sea keeps the schedule. It never loses.
Another hull gone. Same stretch, same weather, same nothing to be done.
They don't say the names on the quay anymore. There are too many for one breath.
Whoever's sinking our boats had better stay out of the harbour. Or in it. I'm undecided.
The shipwrights are working through the night. It's not enough, and they know it.
Half the fleet's down. Half the town knows exactly who they were.
The harbour's shut. Everything we need is sitting just past the mouth, within sight.
Not a sail comes in. The merchants are counting their losses, and the rest of us are counting our meals.
They've closed the water to us. They've picked a very good way to choke a town.
Prices doubled the day the blockade started. Everyone's selling what they can't spare.
We can see their ships at night. They keep their lamps lit, just to remind us.
The dive crews lost another pair yesterday. They'll find a third to take the rope. They always do.
I can't count the widows anymore. The dive-widows have their own corner of the shrine now.
The pay's good for a diver, and short for a funeral. The Compact doesn't mention the funeral.
People say it's a good living. They don't say how short it is.
Nobody asks anymore if the crews are safe. They only ask who's going down next.
You. I haven't forgotten what you did. I don't forget, and I intend to repay it.
Welcome back. The door's open to you, and it is not open to many.
You're the one who stood up for me. I told the others. They didn't believe me, but I knew.
I owe you. Not a debt, exactly. Something heavier and better.
Good to see you. Sit. I don't care what the neighbours think.
You. I'd hoped you'd gone. I haven't forgiven it, and I haven't forgotten it.
Don't smile at me. I remember what you did.
There's nothing to say between us. Say it anyway, if you must, and then leave.
I can still feel it, what you took. Don't expect warmth.
Walk on. The street is wide enough for both of us, but not for the conversation.
I heard what you did for my family. It's not nothing. It's everything, in fact.
My sister told me about you. She doesn't praise easily. I'm listening.
You looked after my own when it mattered. That counts for me as if you'd done it to my face.
Word came. What you did for my kin will be spoken of at this table.
Whatever you need, you've only to say. My family spoke well of you, and mine are hard to please.
You're the one who hurt my kin. Don't think the word hasn't travelled.
I know what happened to my family, and I know whose hand it was.
Stay away from my house. Stay away from my people. This is mercy.
They told me your name. I'd rather they hadn't. Now I can't stop hearing it.
Whatever you did to my family, you did to me. Think about that when you walk away.
I saw what you did. I won't say more, but I saw it.
I was there that day. Everyone says nothing, so I say nothing, but I was there.
Don't ask who saw you. A few of us did. We have chosen what to do with it.
I know more about you than you'd like. I'll keep it, as long as you give me reason.
The whole street saw. They won't say so aloud. They don't need to.
You owe the town, and the town has a long memory. I'm only reminding you.
About what you owe. I'm not asking. I'm simply noting that I know.
The ledger has your name in it, friend. I'd settle it, if I were you.
I don't press. I only mention that a debt grows quietly, like mould.
Every town keeps its accounts. Yours is open. That's all I'll say.
Short of grain again. Naturally. The only thing we're never short of is people telling us to be grateful.
They blockade the harbour and call it policy. I call it the same old hand reaching into the same old pocket.
They'll put up a stone for the divers who die. The living can't eat a stone, but nobody asks the living.
Grain's short, yes, but so is my temper for sorrow. Come, I've a thin soup and a thick joke.
The sea's coming up the steps, and I say let it. It might bring a fish with it.
The sea takes the town an inch at a time. It will be very polite about the last inch.
I knew the men on that hull. I keep thinking they've only gone a little farther than usual.
I've left grain on the altar each night. The gods do not eat it, but the mice have never been better fed.
I said the rites for every hull. The sea has no ears, but I speak for the men.
They say the sea rises because we've displeased someone. I say measure it. It's a number, not a mood.
A hull sank on a black moon. Everyone knows what that means. Nobody will say it.
The sea has begun to climb. It listens to something, and I've stopped asking what.
Prices are splendid, if you're holding stock. I'm sorry for everyone else, naturally.
I'm not hoarding. I'm preserving the value of my property for a time when it's useful. A hard distinction, I know.
I gave my last measure to the Orsen family. We'll make do. Something turns up. It always does.
I've been collecting for the families of the drowned. A coin, a loaf, anything you can spare.
I won't line up at the granary. If it comes to it, I'll eat my pride, and I assure you it's not much of a meal.
I'd run the blockade in a rowboat, if anyone would let me. They won't, so I'm cross instead.
The blockade is the safest the town has ever been. No raiders, no strangers. I like it, and I'm ashamed of liking it.
They asked me to dive. Me! I'd sooner be buried on land, thank you, and I told them as much.
Between us, I heard the hull went down because the master sold the good timber. Nobody's said it. Everyone's thinking it.
Do I know someone who can get past the blockade? I know several. I'll tell you none of them.
If I ever lay hands on whoever ordered this blockade, they'll sleep in the harbour like the fish.
Another hull! I'll tear the shipyard down and rebuild it with my own hands if I have to!
The dive crews are lost at a rate we cannot sustain. I intend to address it. Do not expect speeches.
Grain's short. I've decided to eat my words. They're plentiful, if not very filling.
A blockade! At last, something to make the town's trade interesting. I'd thank them, if I weren't starving.
I've been marking the tide on the harbour wall every day. It's up three finger-widths. I wonder what the sea's trying to say.
I'll stand by every crew that goes down. I'll stand by every widow they leave behind.
They're my people, and the hulls were theirs. I'll rebuild, and I'll do it with them, not for them.
I'm no hero. The crew went down, and I stayed ashore. The least I can do is carry their names.
A blockade is only a very slow wall. Walls fall, if you wait with enough stubbornness.
Hm? Oh. Hello.
Mind the nets, there's one by your foot.
Fair weather, for the moment. Don't trust it.
Another day, then.
Something I can help with, or are you just walking?
The road's quiet. Make of that what you will.
Hello. I'd offer you a seat, but there's only mine.
If you're looking for someone, they're probably at the quay.
Evening's coming on. Watch your step on the stones.
Well. That's the day, isn't it.
